decisionDependencies.role: The existing corpus cannot size a greenfield semantic tier.
The product is polyglot but strategically deep in TypeScript.
Predicates about reachability, authority, and capability require resolved-reference facts.
Rules declare the fact quality they require and shortfall becomes Coverage.

conformanceClaims.claim: No existing-corpus frequency appears in the recommendation.
Resolved-reference or stronger facts are mandatory for predicates whose soundness depends on them.

question: C-1 — Did the semantic-tier inversion overcorrect?

accepted.claim: The 1-of-141 measurement is invalid for greenfield sizing and remains steering evidence only.
Semantic extraction must be a first-class maintained capability, not a rare per-rule compiler-session escape hatch.
Provider-owned semantic universes and batch fact emission are the right state boundary.

rejected.claim: Semantic facts are globally primary for every language with a usable compiler, and syntax-only is globally degraded.
rejected.reason: Fact sufficiency is predicate-relative, not a single total order. A syntax fact can be exact and complete for a local structural predicate; compiler semantics add no truth to it. Conversely, a reachability predicate is unsound without resolved references. A temporarily non-compiling or partially restored worktree can also have authoritative syntax while semantic Coverage is unavailable. Calling all syntax degraded confuses capability breadth with evidence quality.

positiveDerivation.name: predicate-required fact-quality lattice

principles.rule: Each rule/query declares the minimum fact relations, resolution method, confidence, and completeness it needs.
Local-syntactic predicates may be authoritative on syntax facts; semantics is not materialized merely because a compiler exists.
Cross-symbol reachability, authority, type, dispatch, and capability predicates require semantic-quality facts and may not silently fall back.
The planner derives the least sufficient fact view for the selected workload. A profile aggregates requirements and may strengthen them; it cannot weaken a selected rule's minimum.
Provider failure or an unbuildable semantic universe becomes relation-specific Coverage with reasons. Independent syntax-authoritative work may still complete when policy permits.

positiveDerivation.whyThisIsPositive: It follows from soundness per predicate and least-work/least-failure-coupling principles, not from inverting a biased corpus statistic. Semantics becomes normal wherever the product's valuable predicates require it, without taxing or coupling predicates it cannot improve.

reviewOfAgent1Alternatives.ALT-C: partially accept, but profile defaults must be derived from selected predicates rather than hard-coded full/CI/agent-fast labels

costsAndFailureModes: Cold and invalidated semantic-universe construction can dominate interactive latency and memory.
Compiler availability does not imply a stable embeddable provider API or a correctly configured repository.
Dynamic-language type information may be partial and must not be marketed as categorically superior to exact syntax facts.
An always-primary provider turns an unrelated compiler/config failure into a global analysis outage.
Every maintained provider creates toolchain, distribution, compatibility, and false-resolution obligations.

p4SemanticProviderDecision.rationale: TypeScript is the only language positively justified by the sealed product boundary: polyglot breadth with strategically deep TypeScript. The existence of current adapters or of a compiler is not greenfield product evidence for adding another permanent provider.
p4SemanticProviderDecision.otherLanguagesDayOne: Inventory and syntax/reference capabilities with explicit relation-level Coverage; never labelled globally degraded.
admissionCriteriaForAnotherSemanticProvi: A product-owned target-language commitment or measured user workload, not incumbent adapter parity.
Representative-corpus evidence that the provider materially improves false-positive/false-negative or impact quality for named predicates.
A maintainable compiler/language-service API and named ownership for compatibility.
Cold, warm, rebuild, RSS, and partial-project behavior within published workload budgets.
Offline, licensing, signing, and multi-platform distribution feasibility.
Coverage semantics for unresolved, generated, dependency-missing, and non-compiling states.
p4SemanticProviderDecision.reopeningEvidence: A second language with product commitment plus a provider prototype satisfying all admission criteria.

replacementWording: Semantic extraction is a first-class fact capability for languages with a maintained provider. Rules and queries declare predicate-specific fact-quality requirements; the planner materializes the least sufficient fact view and never silently substitutes weaker resolution. Syntax facts can be authoritative for local-syntactic predicates. Resolved-reference, type, reachability, authority, and capability predicates require semantic-quality facts. Profiles aggregate and may strengthen those requirements but cannot weaken them. Provider shortfall is explicit relation-level Coverage, not a global shame label.

agent2Recommendation.decision: Replace primary/degraded wording with the predicate-required fact-quality lattice; select TypeScript alone for day-one semantic depth pending product sign-off.
agent2Recommendation.confidence: high on mechanism; medium on TypeScript-only product scope because no product-demand data beyond the stated boundary is present
